title: Benchmark embedded wasm-git backend
description:
Built the `wasm-git` Meads worktree and branch with an opt-in Git backend using wazero, WASI Preview 1 filesystem mounts, and a 589 KB WASI/libgit2 module built from the sibling wasm-git source.

The embedded backend covers Meads' local object/ref hot path. Network/config/repository-discovery commands and multi-ref `update-ref --stdin` retain the native Git fallback so remote behavior and all-or-none batch semantics remain unchanged.

## Performance (Linux arm64, median of 3 × 1s runs)

- Commit one task ref: native 26.59 ms, WASM 15.64 ms — WASM 1.70× faster.
- Load 100 tasks: native 10.31 ms, WASM 17.50 ms — WASM 1.70× slower.
- Warm-cache backend startup + list one ref: native 1.483 ms, WASM 24.34 ms — WASM 16.4× slower.
- The per-command WASI design allocates heavily; a reactor-style reusable instance is the next performance experiment.

## Verification

- Full `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
- Native/WASM output parity passes for ref writes, CAS conflict classification, batched reads, history, atomic fallback, and linked worktrees.
- Concurrent WASI CAS race admits exactly one winner.
- Real CLI smoke passed init/add/update/get in a temporary repository with `MEADS_GIT_RUNTIME=wasm`.
